blocks.text: Halogenoarenes such as chlorobenzene and bromobenzene are made by reacting benzene with chlorine or bromine in the presence of a catalyst, anhydrous FeCl3 or FeBr3, usually at room temperature. The reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution: C6H6 + X2 -> C6H5X + HX.

blocks.alt: Benzene, with one of its H atoms shown, + X2, with FeX3 over the arrow, gives the halobenzene (X in place of that H) + HX.
blocks.caption: Preparation of halogenoarenes (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 84).
